paper_title: On the Assadi–Liu–Tarjan Auction Algorithm for Bipartite Matching: Simplification, Alternative Analysis, and Hard Instance
classifications: Theory of computation → Streaming, sublinear and near linear time algorithms
Theory of computation → Graph algorithms analysis
statement: In this paper, we advance the understanding of the ALT-algorithm through three contributions. First, we simplify the algorithm by showing that the freezing mechanism as used in its original version by Assadi et al. is unnecessary. Second, we provide an alternative analysis based on augmenting paths, which explains the algorithm’s behaviour more naturally and deals with the removal of the freezing mechanism in a natural way. Third, we construct the first hard instance on which the algorithm indeed requires Ω( ϵ12 ) iterations. We conclude with two open questions. First, and most importantly, are there algorithms that solely rely on the computation of maximal matchings that requires fewer than Θ( ϵ12 ) iterations/matching computations to find a (1 − ϵ)-approximation? Second, can we prove lower bounds for such algorithms? For example, can we show that Ω( 1ϵ ) matching computations are necessary to obtain a (1 − ϵ)-approximation?
